title: Bankei and the Thief
text:
When the Zen master Bankei held his weeks of meditation retreat, pupils came from all over Japan to attend. During one of these gatherings, a pupil was caught stealing. The matter was reported to Bankei, with the request that the culprit be expelled. Bankei ignored the case.

Later the same pupil was caught stealing again, and again Bankei paid no attention. This angered the other pupils. They drew up a petition asking for the thief to be dismissed and declaring that if he was not, they would all leave together.

Bankei read the petition and called everyone before him. "You are wise brothers," he told them. "You know what is right and what is not right. You may go somewhere else to study if you wish, but this poor brother does not even know right from wrong. Who will teach him if I do not? I am going to keep him here even if all the rest of you leave."

Tears poured down the face of the brother who had stolen. All his desire to steal had vanished.
lesson: It is easy to remove the person who causes trouble and harder to help them change. Before you give up on someone, ask whether anyone else will ever teach them.
people: Bankei Yotaku, his pupils, a thieving student
source: 101 Zen Stories, compiled by Nyogen Senzaki and Paul Reps (1919), Right and Wrong
